metaDescription: Odoo for consulting and engineering firms: how retainers, timesheet billing, milestones, utilisation and write-offs are actually configured, and what breaks.
intro: A services firm sells hours and carries them as cost long before anyone pays for them. Odoo has no professional services app. What exists is a set of parts that fit together properly: a service product whose invoicing policy decides how an engagement bills, a project and its analytic account to collect cost, timesheets that value an hour at the employee hourly cost, and a sales order that turns delivered time into revenue.

The configuration that matters most is the service product. Prepaid or fixed price invoices the whole amount on confirmation and drains a balance of remaining hours as timesheets land. Based on timesheets bills what was recorded, in arrears. Based on milestones bills nothing until a stage is marked reached. Three engagements sold in the same meeting but set up differently will produce three different revenue patterns, and the difference is one field on a product.

Community carries more than most buyers assume: Project, Timesheets, Sales with all four invoicing policies, Purchase, Expenses, analytic plans and distribution models, the customer portal and multi-currency. Enterprise buys the timesheet grid with weekly submission and approval, Planning, Documents, Sign, Approvals, Helpdesk, Studio, Subscriptions for recurring retainers, and the asset and deferred entry tools. A utilisation report and a rate card by person are in neither edition.
whoFor: Consulting and advisory firms billing time against a rate card, where the gap between hours recorded, hours billed and cash collected is the entire margin.
Engineering, architecture and design practices on fee-based projects with signed-off stages and a lump sum that has to be recognised across months.
Agencies and IT services companies running retainers, fixed-price builds and time and materials work on the same client account at the same time.
Firms with a partner or director layer whose time is the most expensive input in the business and the least likely to reach a timesheet.
Not for a solo consultant with four clients, where Invoicing on its own does the job and an analytic coding structure is overhead nobody will maintain.
Not for law firms holding client money: a segregated client account, disbursements kept apart from fees and a bill of costs are a separate build, covered on the legal practice page.

capabilities.title: The service product decides the commercial model
capabilities.body: Everything downstream follows from how a service product is configured. The invoicing policy chooses between prepaid or fixed price, billing on recorded timesheets, billing on milestones, and a delivered quantity somebody enters by hand. A second setting decides whether confirming the order creates a task, a project, or both. A firm selling three commercial models needs at least three service products, and serving all of them from one generic consulting line is where the reporting quietly stops working.

capabilities.title: Retainers as a drawdown balance
capabilities.body: A retainer is sold as a prepaid service line for an agreed number of hours. Confirming the order invoices the full fee, and every timesheet posted against the linked task reduces the remaining hours shown on that order line. An account manager can see a client at eighty hours consumed out of a hundred, which is when the overage conversation is worth having. Rolling unused hours into next month is a commercial decision rather than a feature: it is a new line.

capabilities.title: Milestone billing on signed-off stages
capabilities.body: A fixed fee split into stages is sold as one order line per stage with a quantity of one, each tied to a milestone on the project. Marking the milestone reached makes that line invoiceable. Nothing bills automatically, which is correct, because a director signs a stage off before a client sees the invoice. What Odoo will not do is spread the fee across the months the work covered. Revenue lands on the invoice date unless a deferral is posted.

capabilities.title: Cost per hour, and where the number comes from
capabilities.body: A timesheet is worth nothing until the employee has an hourly cost. That field sits on the employee record and drives the analytic line every timesheet writes against the project account, negative for cost. Revenue arrives from the invoice on the same account, so the project profitability view puts both sides together. It is a single current value, so a salary rise changes the cost of hours from that point on and does not restate what is already posted.

capabilities.title: Billable, non-billable, and the hours nobody wants to record
capabilities.body: A timesheet line linked to a sales order line is billable. One posted to an internal project, or to a client project with no order behind it, is not. That single distinction is the whole utilisation report, and it depends on the internal projects existing before go-live: business development, proposal writing, training, internal admin. Create only client projects and every unbilled hour vanishes instead of appearing as a named category somebody can manage.

capabilities.title: Expenses and rechargeable cost
capabilities.body: Travel, hotels, subcontracted specialists and software bought for one client are recorded as expenses or vendor bills carrying the project. A product set to be re-invoiced at cost or at sales price adds itself to the customer order once the expense is approved, so it bills with the next application rather than being remembered a quarter later. Cost that is not rechargeable still posts to the project, which is what keeps job margin honest.

capabilities.title: Capitalised and internal projects
capabilities.body: Internal build work that becomes an asset, an office fit-out, a platform, a piece of test equipment, runs as its own project with its own analytic account, so labour and purchases accumulate against it separately from client work. Odoo does not move that balance into a fixed asset on its own. At the capitalisation date an accountant journals the accumulated cost to the asset account and creates the asset, and the asset and depreciation tooling is Enterprise only.

setup.title: One service product per grade, because there is no rate card
setup.body: Odoo prices a product, not a person. No field makes a partner hour worth three times an analyst hour on the same order line. The pattern that works is a service product per grade, each with its own list price, and a client pricelist layered on top for negotiated rates. Keep the grade list short. Nine grades across four commercial models is thirty-six products somebody has to pick from correctly at order entry, every time.

setup.title: Agree the analytic structure before the first project
setup.body: The project analytic account answers what a job cost. A second plan for the service line or department answers which part of the firm earned it, and a third for the office answers where. Distribution models apply the split automatically from the client, the product or the project so nobody has to type it. Two plans are livable. Five become an entry burden people skip, and recoding a year of posted entries is manual work nobody budgets for.

setup.title: Load work in progress at one cutover date
setup.body: There is no clean way to import an engagement that is half delivered. Take each live job at a single date: contract value, fees billed to date, unbilled time at cost and at charge-out rate, retainer balances still owed to the client, and expenses not yet recharged. Reconcile that to the last client statement before anything is posted. Replaying eighteen months of historic timesheets produces a utilisation history nobody believes and delays go-live by weeks.

setup.title: Make a timesheet take under a minute
setup.body: Adoption decides whether any of the numbers are real. A consultant will complete a day in the mobile timesheet or the my timesheets list if there are three fields and their projects are already assigned to them. The Enterprise grid with weekly submission and a manager approval step earns its licence somewhere above twenty billable staff. Below that, a Friday reminder and a manager who actually reads the report beats any amount of configuration.

setup.title: Fix the capacity number before promising utilisation
setup.body: Utilisation is recorded hours over capacity, and Odoo supplies the numerator only. Capacity comes from the working schedule on each employee, less public holidays and approved leave. Decide whether the denominator is contracted hours or a target of billable days, whether part-timers are pro-rated, and whether leave reduces capacity or counts against it. Two firms running the same pivot with different denominators will report utilisation figures thirty points apart.

setup.title: Decide who may change a delivered quantity
setup.body: The write-down is the most political number in a services firm, and Odoo has no write-off document. The delivered quantity on the order line is editable, so cutting what gets billed is a manual edit that leaves no reason behind it. Agree during design who is allowed to make it, whether the originally recorded hours stay visible on the project, and where the justification is captured, because partners get asked to explain that gap.

pitfalls.title: Every hour posted to one project called Consulting
pitfalls.body: The fastest configuration puts all client work on a single project and removes the reason for doing the implementation. Cost per client, per engagement and per service line collapse into a firm-wide figure the managing partner already had. It happens because nobody wants to create a project per engagement by hand. The fix is the create-on-order setting, which raises the project and the task the moment a quotation is confirmed, so no one has to remember.

pitfalls.title: Partner and director time never recorded
pitfalls.body: The most expensive hours in the firm belong to the people least willing to fill in a timesheet, and their absence does not make projects look better. It makes them look profitable when they are not, because review time, client meetings and rework by a senior person all become free. Either senior time is recorded like everyone else, or the firm should stop treating its project margins as decision-grade. No configuration solves this one.

pitfalls.title: Prepaid retainers billed twice
pitfalls.body: A retainer sold as a prepaid line is invoiced on confirmation. If the same work is then timesheeted against a second order line set to bill on timesheets, those hours bill again. It is not a defect, it is two lines doing two different jobs, and it surfaces as an angry client rather than as an error message. One engagement, one commercial model per line, and an overage line created deliberately when the balance runs out.

pitfalls.title: Expenses recharged from memory
pitfalls.body: Flights, hotels and subcontractor invoices logged outside the project get recharged at quarter end from a folder of receipts, and a share of them are never recharged at all. The expense product has to carry the re-invoice policy and the expense has to carry the project at the moment it is entered, not later. A rechargeable cost that reaches the ledger with no analytic account is money the firm has already decided not to collect.

pitfalls.title: Treating unbilled time as revenue
pitfalls.body: Recorded hours at charge-out rate are not revenue. They are an opinion about what a client will accept, and the distance between the two is realisation. A firm reporting on hours multiplied by rate will forecast a month it does not bill, then spend the following month arguing about the shortfall. Show recorded value, billed value and collected value as three separate figures on one page and manage the gaps rather than hiding them.

regional.note: ZATCA Phase 2 clears every standard invoice through Fatoora before the client ever sees it, so a fee note cannot be issued until the amount is final and the buyer details are complete. Enterprise carries the Saudi e-invoicing integration and Community does not. VAT is 15 percent, fees paid to non-resident consultants are withheld and filed monthly, and staff wages go through WPS.

Corporate tax at 9 percent above the threshold means a consultancy now needs accounts that survive an audit, not only a VAT return. Exported services are zero-rated only where the recipient is genuinely outside the country, which makes place of supply a decision recorded on the engagement rather than an afterthought at invoicing. Wages run through WPS and end of service gratuity accrues per employee.

Sales tax on services is provincial. A Karachi firm billing a Lahore client deals with SRB and PRA under different rates, separate registrations and different return formats, so the tax on a fee line depends on where the service was rendered. FBR digital invoicing pushes documents as they are raised, and clients withhold income tax on professional fees, leaving certificates to match against every receipt.

Professional fees carry GST at 18 percent, and place of supply decides whether that is IGST or a state pair, which bites for a practice with clients in several states. Export of services under a letter of undertaking is zero-rated. E-invoicing applies above the turnover threshold. Clients deduct TDS on professional fees, so cash received is short of the invoice and has to reconcile to the credit statement.

Independent professionals issue a serbest meslek makbuzu rather than an ordinary invoice, and the electronic form, e-SMM, is mandatory for those in scope. Companies send e-Fatura to registered counterparties and e-Arsiv to everyone else, so routing is a decision on each document. Payments for professional work carry withholding, and the statutory Turkish chart of accounts has to be the one in use.

Making Tax Digital requires digital links from the accounting record through to the VAT return, so a spreadsheet in the middle of the process is a compliance problem rather than a habit. Services to business clients abroad fall outside the scope with the customer accounting for the tax. Recharged costs count as disbursements only under a narrow test, and off-payroll rules apply to associates working through their own companies.

Architects and engineers still price against the HOAI structure, where the fee follows construction cost and work phases rather than hours, so the order lines have to be built that way from the start. GoBD requires postings that cannot be altered after the fact, the client accountant will expect a DATEV export, and domestic business invoices now have to be receivable in a structured format such as XRechnung or ZUGFeRD.

VAT on services falls due when the client pays rather than when the invoice is raised, unless the firm has opted for tax on the debits, and that one rule changes the tax point on every fee note. The domestic reform moves invoices to a structured format such as Factur-X through an approved platform, with e-reporting alongside, and the accounting entries file must be produced on request.

faqs.q: Does Odoo have a professional services module?
faqs.a: Not as a single app. A services build is assembled from Sales, Project, Timesheets, Expenses and analytic accounting, which is why two Odoo systems for two consultancies can look nothing alike. The parts fit together properly, and the decisions that matter are the invoicing policy on each service product and the analytic structure beneath it. Anything sold as an Odoo professional services module is third-party code you will end up maintaining.

faqs.q: Can we run this on Odoo Community?
faqs.a: Most of it. Project, Timesheets, Sales with all four invoicing policies, Expenses, analytic plans and distribution models, the customer portal and multi-currency are Community. Enterprise buys the timesheet grid with weekly submission and approval, Planning, Documents, Sign, Approvals, Helpdesk, Studio, Subscriptions, the asset and deferred entry tools, and the localised e-invoicing modules. Firms invoicing under a clearance regime usually find that last item decides the edition.

As a prepaid service line for an agreed number of hours or a fixed monthly fee. The order invoices on confirmation and timesheets draw the balance down, with remaining hours visible on the line, so overage becomes a conversation before it becomes a dispute. Retainers that renew on their own each month need Subscriptions, which is Enterprise. Unused hours do not carry forward unless you decide they should and add a line.

faqs.q: Can Odoo bill different rates for different people on one project?
faqs.a: Not from a single line. There is no per-employee billing rate applied to a timesheet. The working pattern is a service product per grade with its own price, a client pricelist for negotiated rates, and timesheets recorded against the task linked to the right grade. It costs some discipline at order entry, and it is the only version of this that reports correctly at the end of the quarter.

faqs.q: Does Odoo produce a utilisation report?
faqs.a: It produces the numerator. Recorded hours split by billable and non-billable come straight out of the timesheet analysis pivot. Capacity is the part you define: working schedules, public holidays, approved leave, part-time pro-rating, and whether the target is contracted hours or billable days. Once the denominator is agreed the report is a saved pivot or a dashboard rather than a development project.

faqs.q: What happens to time we record but decide not to bill?
faqs.a: It stays on the project as cost and comes off the invoice by reducing the delivered quantity on the order line. There is no write-off document, so the reason lives wherever you choose to put it, usually a note or an activity on the project. Recorded value against billed value is your realisation figure, and it is worth reporting from the first month rather than the first year.

faqs.q: Can clients see progress without us buying them a user licence?
faqs.a: Yes. Portal access carries no licence cost and exists in Community. A client contact signs in to see their quotations, orders and invoices, plus the project tasks shared with them, and can comment on a task instead of emailing the project manager. What each contact reaches is controlled per record, so one client can get invoices only while another follows the work in detail.

faqs.q: Can we capitalise internal project cost?
faqs.a: Cost accumulates against the project analytic account whether the output is billed or capitalised. The step Odoo will not take on its own is moving that balance into a fixed asset. On the capitalisation date an accountant journals the accumulated cost to the asset account and creates the asset record, and the asset and depreciation tooling is Enterprise only. Community users capitalise by journal entry and hold the schedule outside.

faqs.q: How long does an implementation take?
faqs.a: Configuration is measured in weeks. The date is set by two things: whether the firm can agree its grades and rates, and whether people will record time daily. One company with three commercial models and clean opening balances moves quickly. A group with several offices, intercompany recharges and years of unbilled work in progress is a different project, and the work in progress cutover is usually the long pole.
